title: Sakana AI bets AI that improves itself can break the compute arms race of frontier labs
summary_original:
Sakana AI has launched a dedicated research lab for recursive self-improvement: AI that iteratively improves itself. The Japanese startup, co-founded by Transformer co-author Llion Jones, sees RSI as an alternative to the raw compute arms race among big US labs. Anthropic, meanwhile, warns about the control risks of this very technology.

title: Meta's Hatch AI agent could cost up to $200 a month and marks its first paid AI product
summary_original:
Meta is developing a paid AI agent product called "Hatch" that could cost up to $200 per month. Users describe what they need in simple language, and Hatch builds working tools, schedules appointments, or sends emails. CEO Mark Zuckerberg sees the product as a way to open up new revenue streams beyond advertising and refinance the company's massive AI investments.

title: Elon Musk's xAI reportedly trained its coding models on Claude outputs for months before getting cut off
summary_original:
Elon Musk's xAI used Anthropic's Claude to train its own coding models for months and kept going even after Anthropic cut off access, using private accounts and the Blackbox AI service. Meanwhile, xAI's pretraining team shrank to fewer than five people, and several leads walked out. The compute Musk bought up is now being rented to Anthropic and Google instead of powering his own models.

title: SpaceX signs $920 million per month deal with Google for 110,000 Nvidia AI chips ahead of IPO
summary_original:
SpaceX is leasing AI computing capacity to Google for $920 million per month, according to an SEC filing. The deal gives Google access to about 110,000 Nvidia chips to meet demand for its Gemini Enterprise platform. That one of the world's largest cloud providers needs to rent capacity externally shows how scarce AI infrastructure has become, and how tightly big tech companies' businesses are now intertwined.
